role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: experimental design, defining the experimental unit
quote: The mistake that the experimenters have made is that they have not replicated their treatments correctly. They actually have false “replicates” or subsamples.
problem: Researchers treat subsamples within one treated unit as independent replicates (pseudoreplication)
need: Ask what unit received the treatment and set n to the number of experimental units, flagging subsamples

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: Treating subsamples or pseudoreplicates as experimental unit replicates may result in incorrect statistical inference and needlessly increase experimental costs.
problem: Inflated n from subsamples gives wrong inference and wastes effort on the wrong level of replication
need: Design-stage guidance that separates units of analysis from units of replication and averages subsamples

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: comparing two group means from a graph
quote: In this document, we address the following question: can we judge whether two statistics are significantly different based on whether or not their confidence intervals overlap? The short answer is: not always.
problem: Researchers judge significance by eye from overlapping CI/error bars
need: Show the CI of the difference (estimation plot) rather than leaving readers to infer significance from overlapping bars

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: Censoring is an important issue in survival analysis, representing a particular type of missing data. Censoring that is random and non informative is usually required in order to avoid bias in a survival analysis.
problem: Survival data contain censored subjects that ordinary mean comparisons cannot handle
need: A survival data table with an explicit event/censored column and Kaplan-Meier plus log-rank by default

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: choosing a graph type for continuous outcome by group
quote: Bar charts (with or without error bars) are intended to compare magnitude of values, so it is important to always start the y-axis scale at zero.
problem: Choice of graph type and axis range for group comparisons is often wrong (truncated bar charts)
need: Graph defaults that start bar axes at zero and suggest dot/box plots for small samples

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: choosing a graph type for continuous outcome by group
quote: If the data set is small, you can show all the observations grouped by category in a dot plot (Figure 3.1(g)).
problem: Small datasets are summarised as bars when all points could be shown
need: Default to showing all observations for small n

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: repeated measures over time, between and within factors
quote: When the assumption of sphericity is badly violated, the F-statistics and the associated p-values for the within-subject hypotheses have been shown to be inflated, leading to false rejections of the null hypotheses.
problem: Repeated-measures ANOVA p-values are inflated when sphericity fails and users do not apply a correction
need: Apply Greenhouse-Geisser by default and explain it in the output

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: repeated measures with a missing time point
quote: In contrast, in analyzing data in wide format, subjects with even only one missing repeated measurement will be completely excluded from the analysis.
problem: Wide-format repeated-measures ANOVA silently drops any subject with one missing value
need: A mixed-model fit that keeps subjects with missing time points, and a warning when rows are dropped

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: Data sets in either format can be used to analyze data from repeated measures designs. However, there are significant differences in the analysis methods used with each data structure.
problem: Researchers do not know whether to lay repeated-measures data out wide or long, and the choice changes the analysis
need: Accept either layout and convert between wide and long automatically

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: log/sqrt transforming an outcome before ANOVA or regression
quote: Because transformations have multiple effects, their use requires care.
problem: Transforming data to meet assumptions changes interpretation and back-transformed errors become asymmetric
need: Transform options that report back-transformed estimates with asymmetric CIs

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: baseline and follow-up measurement per subject, two groups
quote: Pretest-posttest studies have been pervasive for many years, however many researchers are still unclear on the statistical methods most appropriate for analyzing such data.
problem: Unclear whether to analyse change scores, repeated-measures ANOVA or ANCOVA for before/after designs
need: A test chooser path for baseline-adjusted (ANCOVA) comparison of two groups

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: In the SPSS menus, only post-hoc testing on main effects can be done. In order to do more sophisticated analyses, you need to use the syntax.
problem: Menu-driven software cannot do simple-effects post-hoc comparisons within an interaction
need: Point-and-click simple-effects comparisons (factor A within each level of B) after two-way ANOVA

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: All such data violate the assumption of independence of observations that we typically make in regression models. This is particularly influential on the variability of the model estimates, often resulting in standard errors that are smaller than they should be and thus leading to incorrect inference.
problem: Nested data (cells within animals, repeated measures) analysed as independent gives too-small SEs
need: Nested/hierarchical analysis options (nested t-test/ANOVA, mixed model) surfaced when data are clustered

role: client question to UCLA OARC statistical consulting (shown as "A client has sent us the following question")
quote: I ran a Mann-Whitney test on two independent groups that have equal medians, the results were significant. I thought that the Mann-Whitney tested differences in medians.
problem: Researchers misread what the Mann-Whitney test actually tests (rank sums, not medians)
need: Nonparametric results that state plainly what was compared (mean ranks / distributions) and show medians alongside

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: Choosing a one-tailed test after running a two-tailed test that failed to reject the null hypothesis is not appropriate, no matter how "close" to significant the two-tailed test was.
problem: Researchers switch to one-tailed tests post hoc to reach significance
need: Default two-tailed, require the tail choice to be made and recorded before seeing results

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: However, the p-value presented is (almost always) for a two-tailed test. But how do you choose which test? Is the p-value appropriate for your test?
problem: Users do not know whether the reported p is one- or two-tailed or how to convert it
need: Label every p-value with its tail and let the user pick tails explicitly

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
workflow: choosing a statistical test from design and outcome type
quote: The table below covers a number of common analyses and helps you choose among them based on the number of dependent variables (sometimes referred to as outcome variables), the nature of your independent variables (sometimes referred to as predictors).
problem: "Which test should I use?" is common enough that the consulting group maintains a decision table by number/type of variables and pairing
need: An interactive test chooser that asks outcome type, number of groups, and paired vs independent

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
workflow: moving data entered in Excel into a stats package
quote: Excel is not a statistical package; however, Excel is often the software of choice for inputting data.
problem: Data are entered in Excel and must be moved into a stats tool
need: Robust paste/import from Excel that tolerates typical lab spreadsheets

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
workflow: importing an Excel sheet with a merged header row
quote: If we take a look at our data file, we will immediately see that something went wrong! SPSS appears to have included our row of variable names as an observation in our data file instead of reading them in as variable names like we specified!
problem: Merged header cells and decorative rows in Excel break import
need: Import preview that detects merged/extra header rows and lets the user pick the header row

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
workflow: importing a column with mixed text and numbers
quote: If any further values in that column do not match the format of your first value, SPSS may convert that value to missing (as is the case with observation 9) or it may truncate the information to match the detected format.
problem: Mixed-format cells are silently converted to missing on import
need: Flag non-numeric cells on paste instead of silently dropping them

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: Basically, what we have is a predictor that is the dose of a chemical and a binary response variable that indicates whether the individual dies or not.
problem: Users need LD50/LDp from binary dose-response data and must compute it by hand from logit/probit coefficients
need: Quantal (probit/logit) dose-response fitting that reports LD50/LDx with CIs directly

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: However, using very large effect sizes in prospective power analysis is probably not a good idea as it could lead to under powered studies.
problem: Researchers plug optimistic effect sizes into power calculations and end up underpowered
need: Power tool that asks for effect size in raw units from pilot data and warns on implausibly large effects

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: The CV for a variable can easily be calculated using the information from a typical variable summary (and sometimes the CV will be returned by default in the variable summary).
problem: CV is asked about often and is not always output by default
need: Report %CV in descriptive statistics by default (useful for replicate/assay QC)

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: In this page, we will discuss how to interpret a regression model when some variables in the model have been log transformed.
problem: Interpreting coefficients after log transforms is a recurring question
need: Back-transformed estimates (fold-change / percent change) reported automatically when a log scale is used

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
quote: WARNING: The LOGISTIC procedure continues in spite of the above warning. Results shown are based on the last maximum likelihood iteration. Validity of the model fit is questionable.
problem: Logistic fits on small data hit separation; software continues and prints results anyway
need: Detect separation and explain it in plain language instead of printing questionable estimates

role: course/consulting page, audience: researchers using the UCLA OARC statistical consulting FAQ
workflow: ANOVA with fixed and random factors
quote: One method for determining correct denominators in analysis of variance is the Cornfield-Tukey method.
problem: Choosing the correct error term in ANOVA with random/nested factors is a recurring FAQ
need: Automatic correct F denominators for nested/random factors (e.g. animal within treatment)

role: course/consulting page, audience: clinical and translational investigators preparing for a biostatistics consult (ITHS seminar slides)
workflow: sample size planning for a grant
quote: Power analysis is typically not as easy as plug-and-chug
problem: Investigators expect power analysis to be a quick formula and arrive without the inputs
need: A guided power calculator that asks for the variability estimate and minimum meaningful difference and explains each input

role: course/consulting page, audience: clinical and translational investigators preparing for a biostatistics consult (ITHS seminar slides)
quote: Very important: estimate(s) of variability around yourprimaryoutcome/variables.
problem: Researchers lack a variability estimate for the primary outcome, which every power calculation needs
need: Ways to derive SD from pilot data or published means/SEM/CI inside the power tool

role: course/consulting page, audience: clinical and translational investigators preparing for a biostatistics consult (ITHS seminar slides)
quote: Studies A and B are both “nonsignificant” •Only study B ruled out clinically important differences
problem: Non-significant p-values are read as "no effect" without looking at the CI width
need: Report effect size with CI next to every p-value so non-significance can be judged

role: course/consulting page, audience: clinical and translational investigators preparing for a biostatistics consult (ITHS seminar slides)
quote: Wrongly interpreting odds ratios as probabilities.
problem: Odds ratios are misread as probabilities when results are written up
need: Plain-language interpretation lines under odds ratio / relative risk output

role: course/consulting page, audience: clinical and translational investigators preparing for a biostatistics consult (ITHS seminar slides)
workflow: planning the analysis before data collection
quote: Having a well-defined SAP can save a lot of time in data analysis and also can be used to draft the methods section of your manuscript.
problem: Analyses are improvised after data collection and the methods text is written from scratch
need: Record the planned analysis up front and generate a methods paragraph from what was run

role: course/consulting page, audience: Stanford orthopaedics researchers requesting biostatistics support
workflow: power / sample size for a study or grant
quote: Typically, mean & standard deviation or the proportion observed for your primary outcome(s) previously in similar cohort(s)/sample(s) from the literature
problem: Power calculations need a mean/SD or proportion from prior work that investigators must dig out themselves
need: Power tool that accepts literature summaries (mean, SD/SEM, n) and converts them

role: course/consulting page, audience: Stanford orthopaedics researchers requesting biostatistics support
quote: Data should typically be in one large table with each row containing a patient/sample, and each column containing a variable/outcome
problem: Researchers send spreadsheets in layouts that are not analysable (not one row per sample)
need: Accept tidy (one row per sample) input and convert from grouped/column layouts

role: course/consulting page, audience: Stanford orthopaedics researchers requesting biostatistics support
workflow: cleaning categorical data entered by hand
quote: Example: “no”, “NO”, and “No” are treated as 3 different responses by statistical software, so ensure that capitalization and spelling are consistent
problem: Inconsistent capitalisation of categories splits one group into several
need: Detect near-duplicate category labels on import and offer to merge them

role: course/consulting page, audience: Stanford orthopaedics researchers requesting biostatistics support
quote: Copy and paste as values any data derived from excel formulas after they are calculated to avoid errors creeping in if data is edited/moved; formulas should be listed in the data dictionary
problem: Excel formula-derived values break when data are moved, and the derivation is undocumented
need: Transforms/normalisations computed inside the analysis tool and recorded with the data

role: course/consulting page, audience: Stanford mass spectrometry core users (biostatistics lightning-round slides)
workflow: sample size for a mass-spec / omics experiment
quote: WHAT YOU CAN BRING Statistics • Outcomes: Primary & Secondary • Variability of outcomes • Effect size • Number of samples
problem: Core-facility users come for sample-size help without knowing which inputs are needed
need: Sample-size helper that lists and collects outcome, variability and effect size

role: course/consulting page, audience: Stanford mass spectrometry core users (biostatistics lightning-round slides)
workflow: responding to journal review of statistics
quote: Reviewer comments about statistical analyses
problem: Researchers bring reviewer critiques of their statistics to the consultant
need: Output that documents tests and assumptions well enough to answer reviewer queries

role: course/consulting page, audience: UNM investigators using CTSC biostatistics support
quote: Sample Size/Power Calculations •“How many subjects do I need?” •Bring to your meeting: –Idea of effect size
problem: "How many subjects do I need?" is the headline consulting question
need: Self-serve sample-size calculator with plain inputs

role: course/consulting page, audience: UNM investigators using CTSC biostatistics support
workflow: data collected before consulting a statistician
quote: If you have already collected data without seeking biostatistical advice, expect –A lot of questions from the biostatistician! –Requests for considerable data clean-up on your behalf. –The possibility that the data you have collected may not answer the question(s) intended.
problem: Data collected without design input often need heavy cleanup or cannot answer the question
need: Design-stage guidance (replicates, groups, randomisation) before the experiment is run

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UNC Flow Cytometry Core Facility
quote: Multicolor Flow Cytometry experiments should be run using replicates [be mindful of biological / technical replicates] based on power calculations and include appropriate controls.
problem: Flow users must decide replicate numbers and replicate type without built-in guidance
need: Power/replicate guidance that distinguishes biological from technical replicates for gated percentages

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UNC Flow Cytometry Core Facility
quote: Have a clear and detailed protoco l (SOP) and data analysis plan.
problem: Core asks users to fix a data analysis plan up front and document all analysis steps
need: Analysis log that records every step and setting for the methods section

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the Pediatric/Winship Flow Cytometry Core (Emory/Children's)
quote: For all Multi-color flow cytometry experiments users should run replicates based on Power Calculations .
problem: Core expects power-based replicate numbers that flow users rarely calculate
need: Simple power calculator for proportions/percent-positive endpoints

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UNIL Flow Cytometry Facility (facility newsletter FACS Tips)
workflow: deciding whether a rare gated population is real
quote: This month, in FACS Tips we are answering a recurring question in our facility : Is my population real ? We often have to discuss with users about it and we will provide here an explanation so you can be confident your data is revelant.
problem: Users repeatedly ask whether a small gated population is real
need: Report CI for gated percentages based on event counts and controls

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UNIL Flow Cytometry Facility (facility newsletter FACS Tips)
workflow: choosing how many events to record
quote: Alternatively, if you want to calculate the interval of confidence of your results based on the number of cells acquired and the percentage of your population of interest, you can use the excel tool provided herein.
problem: The facility has to hand out an Excel tool to compute CIs/precision of a gated percentage from event counts
need: Built-in calculator: events needed for a target CV, and CI of a percentage from counts

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the DKFZ Expression Profiling core facility
quote: The same sample on different arrays is considered a technical replicate , but the same treatment (different RNAs) on different arrays is a biological replicate .
problem: "How many replicates?" is the first FAQ, and users confuse technical with biological replicates
need: Replicate-type labels in the data table so technical repeats are averaged and n counts biological replicates

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the DKFZ Expression Profiling core facility
quote: Make sure you involve a statistician in an early phase of your experimental design ("To consult a statistician after an experiment is finished is often merely to ask him to conduct a post mortem examination.
problem: Statistics are considered only after data exist, too late to fix the design
need: Design-time helper (replicates per group, power) before samples are submitted

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the DKFZ Expression Profiling core facility
quote: Also avoid "simple" namings (e.g. 1, 2, 3... or a, b, c...) and reiteration of sample names.
problem: Uninformative or duplicated sample names cause mix-ups between submitted tubes and data
need: Sample metadata columns (group, replicate, animal) rather than ad-hoc names

role: Dorottya Horkai, PhD student, Houseley lab, Babraham Institute (shown)
workflow: learning statistics as a bioscience PhD student
quote: My advice is to never be afraid of doing any statistical analysis, either as you plan experiments or later when analysing your results! Bioscience students are especially guilty of this.
problem: Bioscience students avoid statistics out of fear
need: Approachable, guided analysis that teaches while doing

role: Dorottya Horkai, PhD student, Houseley lab, Babraham Institute (shown)
quote: I have attended one particular course two times before it really became useful, because I had my own data to practice with by the second time.
problem: Statistics courses only stick once the student has their own data to analyse
need: In-tool explanations tied to the user's own dataset rather than generic examples

role: course/consulting page, audience: CU Anschutz campus investigators without statistical expertise (CIDA One Hour Consultation)
quote: While no in-depth analysis of a specific data set can take place during the One Hour Consultation Program, the biostatisticians “can help with talking through how to interpret analysis, or talk through what analysis should be done.”
problem: Investigators without statistical expertise mostly need to know what analysis to run and how to interpret it
need: Guided "what should I run and what does it mean" assistance alongside results

role: course/consulting page, audience: PhD students of biology (Statistics for Biologists workshop, University of Münster)
quote: Tests of statistical significance: which test to use for which question and/or dataset?
problem: Doctoral biologists need to know which test fits their question and data
need: Design-driven test chooser

role: course/consulting page, audience: PhD students of biology (Statistics for Biologists workshop, University of Münster)
quote: What is the difference between standard deviation and standard error? · When to use mean or median?
problem: SD vs SEM and mean vs median remain open questions for biology PhD students
need: Error-bar choice explained at the point of graphing, with SD as default for describing data

role: course/consulting page, audience: PhD students of biology (Statistics for Biologists workshop, University of Münster)
quote: How to design experiments form a statistical point of view (e.g. how many samples and/or experiments do I need to get a significant result)?
problem: Students want to know how many samples/experiments they need
need: Sample-size planning from expected effect and variability

role: course/consulting page, audience: PhD students of biology (Statistics for Biologists workshop, University of Münster)
quote: What are criteria for outliers? How to deal with “irregular” data sets?
problem: No agreed criteria for outliers or for non-normal "irregular" data
need: Documented outlier-detection methods (e.g. ROUT/Grubbs) with a record of what was excluded

role: course/consulting page, audience: PhD students of biology (Statistics for Biologists workshop, University of Münster)
quote: How to illustrate data and statistical results?
problem: Students are unsure how to graph data together with the statistics
need: Graph templates that combine raw points with test annotations

role: course/consulting page, audience: students of STAT 555 Statistical Analysis of Genomics Data (Penn State online notes)
workflow: replication strategy for omics / qPCR follow-up
quote: Technical replication and remeasurement of the same biological samples is typically not cost-effective when making biological inferences.
problem: Labs spend resources on technical rather than biological replicates
need: Planning guidance that shows how SE shrinks with biological vs technical replicates

role: course/consulting page, audience: students of STAT 555 Statistical Analysis of Genomics Data (Penn State online notes)
quote: Many of you have likely read papers where people did a high throughput gene expression study which was followed up with PCR.
problem: qPCR validation of a few high-throughput hits is routine but addresses the technology, not the biology
need: qPCR analysis that works on new biological samples, not just re-measured ones

role: course/consulting page, audience: University of Lincoln students using MASH maths and stats help
quote: One of the biggest challenges students face when doing statistical testing is knowing which test to use in which circumstance.
problem: Knowing which test to use is named the biggest challenge for students
need: Flowchart-style chooser built into the analysis step

role: course/consulting page, audience: University of Lincoln students using MASH maths and stats help
quote: At MASH we understand that this can be very daunting and overwhelming, so we have made these guides to hopefully talk you through the process.
problem: Test selection is daunting and overwhelming for learners
need: Step-by-step guided analysis with plain explanations

role: course/consulting page, audience: Duke Global Health investigators (Research Design and Analysis Core)
quote: If someone had your study dataset and the manuscript, could they reproduce the analysis and obtain the same numerical results?
problem: Published analyses often cannot be reproduced from the data plus the methods text
need: Saved analysis that re-runs from the data and exports exact settings

role: course/consulting page, audience: Duke Global Health investigators (Research Design and Analysis Core)
quote: Not even the most sophisticated statistical fireworks can overcome the limitations of a study that was not designed properly to answer a particular research question.
problem: Poor design cannot be rescued by analysis
need: Design checks (replicates, controls, randomisation) before data collection

role: course/consulting page, audience: Duke Global Health investigators (Research Design and Analysis Core)
quote: Have you considered trying to write your next Discussion section without using the phrase “statistically significant”?
problem: Overreliance on p<0.05 dichotomy in write-ups
need: Results output that leads with effect sizes and CIs

role: course/consulting page, audience: Duke Global Health investigators (Research Design and Analysis Core)
quote: A statistician will know many of the pitfalls of interpretation of study results, such as how odds ratios are commonly misinterpreted, when measurement error may be a bigger problem than confounding, and how conclusions often go beyond what the study design and statistical results allow.
problem: Odds ratios misinterpreted and conclusions overreach
need: Plain-language interpretation of ORs/RRs in output

role: chemistry lab students who came to UVA StatLab consultants (reported in StatLab article)
workflow: many compounds vs one control, one-way ANOVA + post-hoc
quote: Later, they learned that individual t-tests were not appropriate, so they used Dunnett’s test instead. However, they were puzzled: after adding just one more compound to the analysis, a result that had been significant became non-significant.
problem: Users do not understand why adding a group changes other comparisons' adjusted p-values in Dunnett's test
need: Explain multiplicity in the output: show how many comparisons the correction covers and why p changed

role: chemistry lab students who came to UVA StatLab consultants (reported in StatLab article)
quote: The data were analyzed using a one-way ANOVA, and then t-tests between each compound and the control to determine whether the differences were significant—that is, 20-30 comparisons against the control.
problem: Labs run 20-30 uncorrected t-tests after ANOVA
need: Default to Dunnett (vs control) after one-way ANOVA when a control column is marked

role: chemistry lab students who came to UVA StatLab consultants (reported in StatLab article)
quote: Even more confusing, the same effect size was significant in another lab’s analysis but not in theirs.
problem: Same effect significant in one lab and not another because of differing numbers of comparisons
need: Report the family size and correction method alongside each adjusted p

role: course/consulting page, audience: UVA researchers and students (StatLab consulting article)
quote: To maintain power, the number of comparisons should be limited to those essential for the research question.
problem: Including every possible comparison drains power
need: Let users pick only planned comparisons and show the power consequence

role: course/consulting page, audience: UVA researchers and students (StatLab consulting article)
quote: You sometimes see it in analysis flowcharts after a question such as "is your data normal?" A "no" branch off this question will recommend a Wilcoxon test if you're comparing two groups of continuous measures. So what is this Wilcoxon test?
problem: Researchers reach the Wilcoxon test via flowcharts without knowing what it tests
need: Nonparametric result pages that explain the hypothesis tested

role: course/consulting page, audience: UVA researchers and students (StatLab consulting article)
workflow: more than two groups with small n
quote: What if your data doesn’t follow a normal distribution or if your sample size is too small to determine a normal distribution?
problem: Small samples make normality impossible to judge, leaving the parametric vs nonparametric choice open
need: Guidance for small-n normality decisions instead of relying on normality tests

role: course/consulting page, audience: UVA researchers and students (StatLab consulting article)
quote: It’s just a visual check, not an air-tight proof, so it is somewhat subjective.
problem: Assumption checks (QQ plots) are subjective and hard to read
need: Residual QQ plots with plain-language guidance attached to ANOVA/t-test output

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the Utah State University Bioinformatics Core
quote: How many biological replicates are needed? At least 3 (more if you can afford)
problem: "How many biological replicates?" is a standing core-facility FAQ
need: Replicate-number guidance tied to expected variability

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the Utah State University Bioinformatics Core
quote: All the DEG analysis tools are developed based on different normalization methods and assumptions. There is no single tool that can be declared better over other.
problem: Different DE tools give different results because of different normalisation assumptions
need: Transparent statement of normalisation method and a way to compare methods side by side

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the Utah State University Bioinformatics Core
quote: To convert the logFC value from edgeR (which are essentially ratios of the normalized count values per gene) into an up or down ratio, you simply take 2 to the power of the logFC number.
problem: Users need help converting log2 fold-change back to ratios
need: Show both log2FC and linear fold-change in results tables

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UNT Genomics Center (RNAseq Q&A)
quote: More than two biological replicates are required; 3-5 replicates are common choices; and more than 6-12 replicates are recommended (Schurch et al. 2016). However, this question is more appropriate for your statistician.
problem: Replicate number questions are referred on to statisticians because the core cannot answer them generically
need: Self-serve power/replicate estimate using variance and effect size inputs

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Technical versus biological replicates Not always easy to tell the difference • Design 1: One value per glass slide e.g. cell count • After quantification: 6 values • Sample size: n = 1
problem: Six measured values from one culture are often counted as n=6 when n=1
need: Data table that records the replicate hierarchy (day/culture/well) and computes n at the right level

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Identify technical and biological replicates • Make the replicates as independent as possible • Consider wider factors, e.g. rarity of samples, cost and accuracy of measurements • Never mix technical and biological replicates
problem: Labs mix technical and biological replicates within the same analysis
need: Separate replicate-type columns with automatic averaging of technical repeats

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Grants: justification of sample size • Publications: reviewers ask for power calculation evidence
problem: Grants and reviewers demand power calculations that bench scientists struggle to provide
need: Built-in power analysis with a citable report

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Two times easier to reach significance with one-tailed than two-tailed → suspicious reviewer!
problem: One-tailed tests are used to reach significance and attract reviewer suspicion
need: Two-tailed default with justification required for one-tailed

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Not meeting the assumptions for parametric tests is not enough to switch to a non-parametric approach • Data exploration is key: • Outliers? • Possible transformation? • Parametric with corrections?
problem: Researchers switch to nonparametric tests automatically when a normality test fails
need: Guided assumption checking that suggests transformation or corrections before switching tests

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Step by step analysis and considerations: 1. Choose a Model • not necessary to normalise • should choose it when values defining 0 and 100 are precise • variable slope better if plenty of data points
problem: Choosing the dose-response model (normalised or not, variable slope or not) needs explicit guidance
need: Model-choice helper for dose-response that explains normalisation and slope options

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
quote: Problem: very conservative leading to loss of power (lots of false negative)
problem: Bonferroni correction costs power and users do not know the alternatives
need: Correction chooser explaining FWER vs FDR trade-offs

role: course/consulting page, audience: Nelson Mandela University postgraduates and researchers (Unit for Statistical Consultation FAQ)
workflow: sample size for an ethics application
quote: Q: I need to figure out my required sample size for my study to include in my ethics application/proposal, can the USC help me with that?
problem: Sample size is needed for ethics/proposal paperwork before the researcher understands how to compute it
need: Sample-size calculator with an exportable justification paragraph for ethics forms

role: course/consulting page, audience: Nelson Mandela University postgraduates and researchers (Unit for Statistical Consultation FAQ)
quote: It is important to note that you need a clear understanding of your research design before you can determine the sample size necessary for your study.
problem: Researchers ask for n before the design is settled
need: Power tools that start by capturing the design (groups, pairing, outcome type)

role: course/consulting page, audience: Nelson Mandela University postgraduates and researchers (Unit for Statistical Consultation FAQ)
quote: Unfortunately, while it may seem that it will only take a few minutes, in most cases the question needs a significant amount of time to answer.
problem: "Quick" statistics questions are rarely quick; consultants are a bottleneck (2 consultants for the whole university)
need: Self-service guidance that answers the common questions without a consultant

role: course/consulting page, audience: Nelson Mandela University postgraduates and researchers (Unit for Statistical Consultation FAQ)
quote: Once you have finished writing up your results chapter, your consultant will be able to read through it to ensure that the statistical results are correctly written up and interpreted.
problem: Students need their write-up of statistical results checked for correct interpretation
need: Auto-generated results sentences with correct statistic, df and p formatting

role: course/consulting page, audience: JKU Linz medical faculty researchers (statistical consulting FAQ)
workflow: what researchers come to consultants for
quote: The Team Statistics helps with: study design and sample size calculation writing the statistical analysis plan writing the biometry section of the application for the ethics committee answering questions regarding the data acquisition selecting appropriate statistical methods
problem: Consulting demand centres on sample size, analysis plans, ethics biometry sections and method choice
need: Tooling for method selection and sample-size justification text

role: course/consulting page, audience: bioimage analysis users (Crick imaging and bioinformatics facility staff guidance, Journal of Cell Science 2026)
workflow: quantifying microscopy images and testing differences
quote: In particular, the use of appropriate controls and experimental repetition is critical for drawing meaningful conclusions. However, there are times when both are inadequately applied or overlooked in favour of 'statistical significance', often derived from misused or misinterpreted statistical tests.
problem: Image-analysis results lean on p-values from misused tests instead of proper repetition and controls
need: Image-derived data analysed per experiment (superplot style) with effect sizes

role: course/consulting page, audience: bioimage analysis users (Crick imaging and bioinformatics facility staff guidance, Journal of Cell Science 2026)
quote: We also discuss the diminishing returns of increased data collection once statistical stability has been achieved.
problem: Imaging users collect ever more cells expecting more certainty
need: Show how precision changes with more cells vs more independent experiments

role: course/consulting page, audience: Northwestern investigators (Biostatistics Collaboration Center "Statistically Speaking" lecture slides)
workflow: comparing time to event between treatment groups
quote: Compare mean time between groups - T-test, linear regression? - Not normally distributed - Ignores subjects without events
problem: Researchers compare mean time-to-event with t-tests, ignoring censored subjects
need: Route time-to-event data to Kaplan-Meier/log-rank automatically

role: course/consulting page, audience: Northwestern investigators (Biostatistics Collaboration Center "Statistically Speaking" lecture slides)
quote: Interpretation of Hazard Ratio depends on how you code your variables!
problem: Hazard ratio direction depends on reference coding and is easily misread
need: State the reference group explicitly next to every hazard ratio

role: course/consulting page, audience: Northwestern investigators (Biostatistics Collaboration Center "Statistically Speaking" lecture slides)
quote: What if last observation is censored? Survival Time (Days) Survival Probability Day At risk Events Estimate 7 8 1 0.875 12 5 1 0.700 15 4 1 0.525 20 2 0 -- 22 1 0 -- Median failure time not always estimable
problem: Median survival can be undefined when the curve does not reach 50%, which confuses users
need: Report "undefined" medians clearly with an explanation

role: course/consulting page, audience: Northwestern investigators (Biostatistics Collaboration Center "Statistically Speaking" lecture slides)
quote: Proportional hazards assumption - Hazard functions are proportional over time - Covariate effect is constant over time
problem: Proportional hazards assumption must be checked but is often not
need: Built-in PH check (log-log plot / test) with Cox and log-rank output

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UVA Flow Cytometry Core Luminex service (FAQ)
workflow: multiplex bead assay, standard-curve interpolation of analyte concentrations
quote: How do I interpret the data? o Generally, users will receive two excel documents: a Detailed report and a Summary report.
problem: "How do I interpret the data?" is a core FAQ; results arrive as two large Excel reports
need: Import of multiplex reports with standard-curve fits, interpolated concentrations and replicate CVs in one view

role: course/consulting page, audience: users of the UVA Flow Cytometry Core Luminex service (FAQ)
workflow: checking replicate agreement in multiplex assays
quote: This report is very large and is used for troubleshooting, such as looking at samples with high CVs between the two replicates.
problem: Finding duplicate wells with high CV requires digging through a very large detailed report
need: Automatic flagging of high-CV replicate pairs and out-of-range interpolations

role: course/consulting page, audience: University of Sheffield students and researchers (MASH statistics help)
quote: It can be difficult to know what analysis to perform on your dataset. This page is designed to help you.
problem: Students find it difficult to know which analysis fits their dataset
need: Test chooser driven by data types and design

role: course/consulting page, audience: University of Sheffield students and researchers (MASH statistics help)
quote: Variables can be classified as continuous, categorical, ordinal etc. Usually one variable is an outcome / dependent variable while you may have several predictor / independent variables.
problem: Users must first classify variables (outcome vs predictor, continuous vs categorical) before any test choice
need: Data-table types that capture outcome/predictor roles so test choice follows

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cambridge graduate biologists (Statistics for Graduate Biologists course outline)
quote: REMEMBER - DECIDE ON YOUR STATISTICAL PROCEDURES WHEN DESIGNING YOUR PROJECT, BEFORE YOU COLLECT THE DATA
problem: Graduate biologists choose statistics after collecting data
need: Design-stage planning tool that fixes the analysis before data collection

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cambridge graduate biologists (Statistics for Graduate Biologists course outline)
workflow: complex designs beyond a basic course
quote: For more complex statistical problems, you should be able to design experiments and surveys, and analyse your data correctly, on the basis of specialist advice.
problem: Complex designs (nested, factorial) still need specialist help after a full course
need: Guided support for nested/factorial designs common in biology

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
quote: Students often go straight to the hypothesis test rather than investigating the data with summary statistics and charts first.
problem: Users jump to a test without looking at the data, missing outliers and skew
need: Show descriptive stats and a points plot before any test result

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
quote: There are statistical tests for normality such as the Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnoff tests but for small sample sizes (n < 20), the tests are unlikely to detect non-normality and for larger sample sizes (n > 50), the tests can be too sensitive.
problem: Normality tests are unreliable at the small n typical of lab work yet drive test choice
need: De-emphasise normality-test p-values for small n; show QQ plots and guidance

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
workflow: running many tests on one dataset
quote: Some students will try to perform a large number of tests on their data. The chance of a type I error increases with the number of tests.
problem: Many uncorrected tests inflate false positives
need: Track the number of comparisons and offer correction

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
quote: The most commonly used post hoc tests are Tukey and Sidak although Scheffe’s is often used in medicine. Suggest that the student looks in their notes or papers in their field when choosing.
problem: Post-hoc test choice is made by field convention rather than design
need: Post-hoc recommendation based on which comparisons are planned (all pairs, vs control, selected)

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
quote: Some departments routinely use parametric tests to analyse ordinal data.
problem: Ordinal scores (e.g. histology scores) are analysed with parametric tests by department habit
need: Flag ordinal/score outcomes and suggest rank-based tests

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
quote: If the assumption is not met, the F-statistic is positively biased leading to an increased risk of a type 1 error.
problem: Sphericity violations in repeated measures ANOVA inflate false positives
need: Automatic Greenhouse-Geisser correction with a plain explanation

role: course/consulting page, audience: students of STAT 503 Design of Experiments (Penn State online notes)
quote: However, as most practicing statisticians quickly learn, typically problems that arise at the analysis stage, could have been avoided if the experimenter had consulted a statistician before the experiment was done and the data were conducted.
problem: Analysis-stage problems stem from designs made without statistical input
need: Design checks before the experiment

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: chi-square test on a larger contingency table
quote: When a significant association is detected in a large table, interpretations can be difficult. In this document, we will present a method for performing post-hoc tests on a contingency table that is easy to interpret.
problem: After a significant chi-square on a large table users cannot tell which cells drive it
need: Adjusted standardised residuals / cell-wise post-hoc output for contingency tables

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: Equivalence testing should not be confused with the more familiar method of significance testing for comparing two population means.
problem: Researchers treat a non-significant difference as proof of equivalence
need: Equivalence (TOST) option with a user-set margin

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
quote: Each technique results in the same overall fit to the data, but the hypotheses tested by the computer-generated output are not necessarily the same.
problem: ANOVA and regression output test different hypotheses with unbalanced cells (type I vs III SS), confusing users
need: State the sums-of-squares type and hypotheses tested in two-way ANOVA output

role: course/consulting page, audience: Cornell researchers (CSCU consulting handout)
workflow: batches, plates or runs as factors
quote: Most statistical analyses will incorporate these sources of variation as explanatory variables or “factors” in a statistical model.
problem: Users must decide whether batch/run/plate is a fixed or random factor
need: Guided choice of blocking/random factor (e.g. experiment day) in ANOVA

role: course/consulting page, audience: Babraham Institute scientists (Introduction to Statistics with GraphPad Prism course slides)
workflow: choosing error bars for a graph
quote: SD or SEM ? • If we want to show the variation among values: → Report the SD • If we want to show how precisely we have determined the population mean: → Report the SEM • Preferably show all data points and the SEM
problem: SD vs SEM error bar choice is a recurring question
need: Graphs that show all points plus a labelled error bar, with the bar type written into the legend

role: course/consulting page, audience: maths/statistics support tutors helping students (statstutor quick guide)
quote: 80% of expected cell counts >5 SPSS tells you under the test Fisher’s exact (usually for 2x2 tables, but can also be used for others) or merge categories where sensible
problem: Small expected counts invalidate chi-square and users must switch to Fisher or merge categories
need: Automatic expected-count check that recommends Fisher exact

role: course/consulting page, audience: life scientists using GraphPad Prism (Babraham Institute training course)
workflow: in vivo, several measurements per animal
quote: What to do? Not one good answer ... In this case: mouse = experiment unit, nerve segments = biological replicates, axons = technical replicates
problem: Nested measurements (axons within nerve segments within mice) have no single obvious n
need: Support nested/hierarchical data entry and offer a nested analysis (or per-animal summary) instead of treating every axon as independent

role: course/consulting page, audience: life scientists using GraphPad Prism (Babraham Institute training course)
quote: Never ever interpret p-values without context! ... Not big enough = underpowered: potentially a false negative/type 2 error
problem: Non-significant results from small samples are read as 'no effect'
need: Report the effect size with its CI next to every p-value and flag likely underpowered comparisons

role: course/consulting page, audience: life scientists using GraphPad Prism (Babraham Institute training course)
quote: Proper power calculations need to specify which kind of distribution we are dealing with – not easy ... Compute sample size required for a parametric test and add 15%
problem: Power for non-parametric tests is hard; trainees are given a crude rule of thumb
need: Offer sample-size estimates for rank-based tests (with the +15% rule or simulation) rather than leaving users to improvise

role: course/consulting page, audience: life scientists using GraphPad Prism (Babraham Institute training course)
quote: Running multiple tests on the same data increases the familywise error rate ... For comparisons between 5 groups, the familywise error rate is 40%
problem: Users run many uncorrected pairwise t-tests after ANOVA
need: Route multi-group comparisons through a corrected post-hoc procedure by default and show the familywise error rate if uncorrected tests are chosen

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
workflow: animal and cell experiments with sub-sampling
quote: Pseudoreplication is a common and serious problem. Pseudo-replication occurs when an analysis treats a dataset as if the sample size is larger than is appropriate.
problem: Analyses treat non-independent measurements as separate samples, shrinking p-values
need: Detect repeated rows from the same subject/culture and warn that n is inflated before running a test

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: "But, isn't the sample size simply equal to the number of measurements that were made?". The answer is, "Sometimes yes, sometimes no."
problem: Students assume sample size equals number of measurements
need: Ask for the unit of randomisation at data entry and show n per that unit

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: researchers often use a Mann-Whitney U test to analyse data that fail to meet the assumptions of a t-test; here, researchers aim to evaluate evidence that the median values differ between the groups ... if two distributions being compared differ in shape, then a small p-value might arise from a Mann-Whitney U test (at least in part) due to shape differences
problem: Mann-Whitney is used as a 'median test' when distributions differ in shape
need: When a rank test is chosen, state what hypothesis it actually tests and offer bootstrap/permutation CIs for the median difference

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: This idea of ‘significance’ is commonly ingrained in interpretation of statistical tests in biology. But, it turns out that this approach leads to serious errors.
problem: Results are reduced to significant/not significant at p<0.05
need: Report exact p-values and effect sizes with 95% CI as the primary output, not asterisks alone

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: a power analysis based on standard software can easily lead a researcher to design a study that has high power to detect a factor’s overall effect, but lower power when conducting post-hoc tests.
problem: Standard power software sizes ANOVA studies for the omnibus F, not the pairwise comparisons researchers care about
need: Power analysis for multi-group designs at the level of the planned post-hoc contrasts (simulation-based)

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: In short, low-powered studies cannot be trusted. This begs the question, how often are studies insufficiently powered? As we discuss, at least within the biological sciences, it appears that most published studies are underpowered.
problem: Most biology studies are underpowered and their effect sizes inflated
need: Show achieved precision (CI width) and warn when n is too small to detect the smallest effect of biological interest

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: This video provides a general introduction to 1-factor GLM (1-way ANOVA), and addresses the question, "Why shouldn't we analyse an experiment with lots of treatments with many t-tests?"
problem: Experiments with many treatments are analysed with a series of t-tests
need: Detect >2 groups and steer the user to one model plus corrected contrasts

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
workflow: two-factor experiment (drug x sex, genotype x treatment)
quote: my experience suggests that the field of Biomedical Sciences less frequently addresses hypotheses involving interactions ... a 2-factor GLM can only include an ‘interaction term’ if the experiment has appropriate replication
problem: Biomedical researchers rarely test interactions (e.g. drug x sex) and may lack replication to do so
need: Two-way ANOVA output that leads with the interaction, explains it in words, and checks the design has replicates per cell

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: appropriate analyses can require more sophisticated models than simply including ‘subject’ as a random effect (often the first instinct for many researchers). For example, when measurements within subjects are more similar between points closer in time than between those more distant points in time, ‘autocorrelation’ can increase type 1 errors
problem: Time-course data are analysed with a random intercept only, ignoring autocorrelation
need: Repeated-measures/time-course module that offers correlation structures beyond a random subject effect and explains when they matter

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: if our experiment involved repeatedly measuring subjects, families, individuals within cages (etc), our analysis would suffer from pseudo-replication if we did not account for the non-independence of the repeated measurements.
problem: Cage, litter and repeated-subject structure is ignored in analysis
need: Let users tag a grouping column (cage, litter, animal) and fit it as a random effect automatically

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: we walk through an example of plotting data for experiments with several treatments and focus on the need to display all of the data (not merely mean values) to communicate results transparently.
problem: Figures show only means
need: Default graphs that overlay individual points on summary statistics

role: course/consulting page, audience: biomedical science students and researchers (University of Edinburgh)
quote: The importance of ‘blinding’ throughout an experiment; studies that lack blinding can yield surprisingly biased results.
problem: Experiments are run unblinded and unrandomised
need: Provide a randomisation/blinding helper (random allocation and coded group labels) linked to the data table

role: course/consulting page, audience: university researchers who consult the UVA Library StatLab
quote: I always checked normality for each variable and made sure they were normally distributed before running any analyses, such as t-test, ANOVA, or linear regression. ... No, you don’t have to transform your observed variables just because they don’t follow a normal distribution.
problem: Researchers test raw variables for normality instead of model residuals
need: Run assumption checks on residuals of the fitted model and explain what the check means

role: course/consulting page, audience: university researchers who consult the UVA Library StatLab
quote: The idea is to show that a “non-significant” hypothesis test failed to achieve significance because it wasn’t powerful enough.
problem: Researchers compute 'observed power' after a non-significant result
need: Do not offer post hoc observed power; offer CI of the effect and a prospective power calculation instead

role: course/consulting page, audience: university researchers who consult the UVA Library StatLab
quote: Why do this? One reason is to make data more "normal", or symmetric. ... But while it's easy to implement a log transformation, it can complicate interpretation.
problem: After log-transforming skewed data, users cannot interpret the coefficients
need: When a log transform is applied, back-transform results and state them as fold/percent changes

role: course/consulting page, audience: university researchers who consult the UVA Library StatLab
quote: We sometimes want to make pairwise comparisons to see where differences occur. ... Making multiple comparisons leads to an increased chance of making a false discovery
problem: Pairwise comparisons of several proportions are run without adjustment
need: Contingency module with adjusted pairwise proportion comparisons after the overall chi-square/Fisher test

role: course/consulting page, audience: university researchers who consult the UVA Library StatLab
quote: You ran a linear regression analysis and the stats software spit out a bunch of numbers. The results were significant (or not). You might think that you’re done with analysis. No, not yet.
problem: Users stop at the p-value without checking residuals
need: Show residual/QQ diagnostics automatically with every fit and flag clear violations

role: course/consulting page, audience: university researchers who consult the UVA Library StatLab
quote: Neither appear to have any effect on the mean response value. But what about their interaction? ... The effect of trt depends on gender.
problem: Main effects can look null while a strong interaction exists
need: Two-way ANOVA output with an automatic interaction plot and plain-language interpretation

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Show your data! Dynamite plot Awful! Box plot OK Jitter plot Better Beeswarm plot Best!
problem: Dynamite plots (bar + error bar) hide the data
need: Make beeswarm/box-with-points the default for small-sample group comparisons, not bars

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Make sure error bars are visible ... Always state what type of uncertainty is represented by your error bars
problem: Error bars are unlabelled or hidden behind bars
need: Auto-insert error-bar type (SD/SEM/95% CI) and n into the legend; always draw both arms

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: There is no zero in a logarithmic scale! ... Bar size depends on an arbitrary lower limit of the vertical axis ... Don’t do it!
problem: Bar charts are drawn on log axes where bar length is meaningless
need: Warn or switch to points when the user puts bars on a log axis

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Make your plots colour-blind friendly ... Colour-blindness affects about 8% men and 0.5% women
problem: Default palettes (red/green) are not colour-blind safe
need: Ship a colour-blind-safe default palette (e.g. Okabe-Ito)

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: If you publish a p<0.05 result, you have a 36% chance of making a fool of yourself
problem: p<0.05 is treated as proof although the false discovery rate can be far higher
need: Present p as a continuous measure with effect size and avoid binary 'significant' labels by default

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Underpowered studies lead to unreliable p-values ... When your experiment is underpowered, you are screwed
problem: Small-n experiments give unreliable p-values and inflated effects
need: Warn when power for the observed design is low and show CI width rather than a bare p

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Data dredging, p-hacking ... Searching until you find the result you were looking for ... Let’s try again
problem: Researchers repeat or re-analyse until p<0.05 (p=0.06? let's try again)
need: Keep an analysis log of every test run on a dataset so unreported tests and re-runs are visible

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Never, ever say that large p supports H0 ... Reporting a discovery based only on p<0.05 is wrong
problem: Large p-values are reported as evidence of no difference
need: Phrase non-significant results as 'inconclusive' with the CI of the effect in generated text

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: My recommendation: do not perform normality test before ANOVA ... underpowered for small samples (many false negatives) ... oversensitive for large samples (many false positives)
problem: Users gate ANOVA on a Shapiro-Wilk test that is uninformative at small and large n
need: Do not auto-switch tests on a normality-test p-value; show residual plots and suggest transforms or Welch

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: doesn’t work for small samples, only 5 discrete p-values for n=3
problem: Rank/permutation tests cannot reach significance with n=3 per group, but biologists choose them for small samples
need: Warn when a non-parametric test is chosen for tiny n and show the minimum attainable p-value

role: course/consulting page, audience: biologists attending the Dundee Data Analysis Group statistics workshop
quote: Breaksdown for small numbers (total count < 100) ... For small numbers use the exact multinomial (or binomial) test
problem: Chi-square is applied to small counts where it is inaccurate
need: Automatically recommend Fisher/exact tests when counts are small

role: institute guidance page, audience: animal and in vitro researchers (UK NC3Rs)
quote: commonly used terms such as “biological” and “technical” replicates, which are frequently used to refer to genuine replication and sub-sampling (see below), respectively, but are often inconsistently defined or misapplied
problem: The words biological/technical replicate are used inconsistently and hide what n is
need: Use the experimental unit / observational unit vocabulary in the data-entry wizard instead of ambiguous replicate labels

role: institute guidance page, audience: animal and in vitro researchers (UK NC3Rs)
quote: Pseudoreplication does not increase the sample size of an experiment, even if there are more data points. ... To address this, you can average the sub-samples for each experimental unit.
problem: Sub-samples (multiple measurements per unit) are entered as independent data points
need: One-click aggregation of sub-samples to one value per experimental unit before testing

role: institute guidance page, audience: animal and in vitro researchers (UK NC3Rs)
quote: If only one biological unit (e.g. a single cell line) is used, it is unclear how applicable the findings are beyond that unit.
problem: Conclusions are generalised from a single cell line
need: Record the biological unit in the methods summary and flag single-line designs in the generated text

role: institute guidance page, audience: animal and in vitro researchers (UK NC3Rs)
quote: The experimental and biological unit should be clearly identified for each experiment. ... It ensures that the sample size for each experiment is clear.
problem: Papers do not state the experimental unit so n is ambiguous
need: Auto-generate a methods/legend sentence stating the experimental unit and n per group

role: core facility guidance page, audience: clients of University of Vermont shared resource cores
quote: Consult with core staff for best practices regarding image processing and analysis. ... Consult with core staff regarding ethical standards for image manipulation.
problem: Core clients need guidance on image processing and acceptable manipulation before quantifying
need: Keep a record of every image-processing step applied before quantified values enter the analysis

role: core facility newsletter, audience: users of the UNIL Flow Cytometry Facility
quote: How many events do I need to record? When performing a flow cytometry experiment, often samples are just run to completion. ... It is also possible that we may be under sampling
problem: Users do not know how many events to acquire for a rare population
need: Calculator for events needed from population frequency and target CV (Poisson), with CI for the observed %

role: institute training module (case study discussion), audience: NIH-funded trainees and postdocs
quote: Have you ever had data that was “close” to significance? If so, what did you do? ... Would Dr. Fielding (Harry) have suggested adding a few more samples and trying a different statistical test if they had initially defined their sample size and exclusion criteria
problem: Near-significant results lead to adding samples and switching tests
need: Pre-register sample size, test and exclusion rules in the project and flag later changes

role: institute training module (case study discussion), audience: NIH-funded trainees and postdocs
quote: Jamal told Robin to drop outliers above a certain value, as it is outside the physiologic range. ... Do you think they actually developed exclusion criteria, or just considered that point as valid
problem: Outliers are dropped ad hoc without predefined exclusion criteria
need: Outlier handling that requires a stated rule, keeps excluded points visible and reports them

role: maths and stats support guide, audience: Sheffield Hallam University students and researchers
quote: Comparing the mean difference of two measurements of the same continuous variable. You should have measurements in different columns with each row representing one subject.
problem: Paired data must be laid out one subject per row, which users often get wrong
need: Data-table template for paired/repeated designs that enforces one row per subject

role: maths and stats support guide, audience: Sheffield Hallam University students and researchers
quote: We don't currently have resources on this topic in Jamovi so book an appointment to see a stats tutor
problem: No self-serve help for repeated-measures ANOVA/Friedman in the free tool, so users must book a tutor
need: Guided repeated-measures ANOVA and Friedman test with step-by-step help in the tool

role: biostatistics core reference sheet, audience: Rush University investigators
quote: some of these types of analyses (logistic regression, linear mixed effects modeling, survival analysis, etc.) can be quite complex and complicated to interpret, and we strongly recommend you come to us at the Rush Biostatistics Core
problem: Logistic, mixed-effects and survival models are hard for investigators to fit and interpret alone
need: Guided set-up and plain-language interpretation for logistic, mixed and survival models

role: biostatistics core reference sheet, audience: Rush University investigators
quote: if the assumptions are severely violated, there are alternative nonparametric tests that may be used instead ... We strongly encourage investigators to consult the Rush Biostatistics Core when choosing between these methods.
problem: Choosing between parametric and non-parametric versions requires a consultation
need: Assumption-aware chooser that explains the trade-off when proposing the non-parametric alternative

role: training aide-memoir on dose-response curve fitting, audience: pharmacology trainees (UCD 3DNet)
quote: REMEMBER - Curve fitting packages are not intelligent and results must be scrutinised. ... Where ever possible use an unconstrained (4-parameter) fit
problem: Curve-fit output is accepted without scrutiny
need: Dose-response fit report with QC checks (plateaus defined, sensible slope, CI width) and warnings

role: training aide-memoir on dose-response curve fitting, audience: pharmacology trainees (UCD 3DNet)
quote: If you must constrain parameters, constrain only one parameter, if two parameters need constraining then the data needs regenerating with a more appropriate concentration range.
problem: Users constrain several parameters to rescue poor concentration ranges
need: Warn when more than one parameter is constrained and suggest extending the concentration range

role: training aide-memoir on dose-response curve fitting, audience: pharmacology trainees (UCD 3DNet)
quote: If the experiment is inherently variable generate more determinations n=3 or 4. Four pieces of independent information are better than curves with quadruplicate points.
problem: Replicate wells within one curve are treated as replication instead of independent determinations
need: Summarise IC50 across independent experiments (e.g. mean log IC50 with CI) rather than pooling replicate points

role: training aide-memoir on dose-response curve fitting, audience: pharmacology trainees (UCD 3DNet)
quote: This example of poor lower asymptote estimate underestimates the true IC50 value for the compound. ... Data should run from 100% to 0% control, with a slope of 1 when the interaction is simple competitive one-site.
problem: Poorly defined plateaus or unmatched controls bias IC50
need: Flag fits whose plateaus are extrapolated and check normalisation controls (0%/100%)

role: training aide-memoir on dose-response curve fitting, audience: pharmacology trainees (UCD 3DNet)
quote: Note that the final values depend on the initial values, so repeated analysis may give slightly different results
problem: Nonlinear fits can return different results on re-running
need: Deterministic, documented initial-value strategy so the same data give the same fit

role: lab guidance FAQ, audience: lab members running standard curves (UNC)
quote: A standard curve should be run for every plate or sample run. ... is whether the plate reader or fluoro-/lumino-meter is set to automatically change the reading values based on the maximum fluorescent intensity observed in the plate.
problem: Standard curves reused across plates despite plate-to-plate and auto-gain variation
need: Tie each standard curve to its plate and interpolate samples only against their own plate's curve

role: lab guidance FAQ, audience: lab members running standard curves (UNC)
quote: Your concentration range should be well distributed with two or more samples above and below your estimated sample concentration.
problem: Samples are interpolated near the edge of, or outside, the standard range
need: Flag samples outside or at the edge of the standard range (LLOQ/ULOQ) and suggest dilution

role: lab protocol wiki, audience: lab members running qPCR (university lab)
quote: Reference genes need to be stable across your control and experimental samples in order to be useful. If expression between the two differs, you will be normalizing to two different values.
problem: Unvalidated reference genes distort ddCt normalisation
need: Reference-gene stability check (across conditions) before computing ddCt

role: lab protocol wiki, audience: lab members running qPCR (university lab)
quote: Technical replicates with a standard deviation below 0.2. ... The first few times you run qPCR the results can be messy, and sometimes you have to redo things to get accurate results.
problem: Messy technical replicates in early qPCR runs
need: Flag technical-replicate Cq SD above a threshold before averaging

role: institute analysis-tool help page, audience: qPCR users (INRAE)
quote: The design of your experiment is describing the number of biological samples including your biological control, the number of technical replicates, and the number of genes tested ... All samples from the same biological replicate have to be in a same block,
problem: qPCR analysis requires a specific layout encoding biological vs technical replicates
need: qPCR import that captures biological replicate, technical replicate and gene as explicit columns

role: institute analysis-tool help page, audience: qPCR users (INRAE)
quote: This validation is done using calibration curves with at least 5 dilution points. The efficiency of the PCR reaction should be between 90-100% with an R2 between 0.99-1.
problem: Primer efficiency must be validated before relative quantification
need: Efficiency calculation from dilution series with efficiency-corrected (Pfaffl) quantification

role: research support unit teaching article, audience: clinicians and researchers (NUS Research Support Unit)
quote: This is another common mistake – researchers at times refer to odds ratio in survival analysis (mistaken by the same symbol).
problem: Hazard ratios are mislabelled as odds ratios
need: Label exp(B) correctly as hazard ratio in Cox output and in generated text

role: research support unit teaching article, audience: clinicians and researchers (NUS Research Support Unit)
quote: We observe that the median survival time has increased from 12 months (without censoring) to 32 months.
problem: Ignoring censoring badly underestimates median survival
need: Survival data entry that requires an event/censor flag and computes Kaplan-Meier medians

role: research support unit teaching article, audience: clinicians and researchers (NUS Research Support Unit)
quote: When the proportional hazard assumption is not satisfied, we will have to use Cox regression with time-dependent covariate to analyse the data.
problem: Proportional hazards assumption is not checked
need: Automatic proportional-hazards check (log-minus-log or Schoenfeld) with a warning

role: IACUC guidance page, audience: animal researchers at UC Davis
quote: the number of animals can be determined by a power analysis (sample size estimation), which is identified by the variability in the data (e.g., Standard Error of the Mean, SEM) and the difference the investigator might anticipate between groups.
problem: Institutional guidance suggests using the SEM as the variability input to power analysis (power needs the SD)
need: Power calculator that asks for SD explicitly and converts SEM to SD with n when users enter SEM

role: IACUC guidance page, audience: animal researchers at Lehigh University
quote: When the animal is not the experimental unit, determine the appropriate sample size for your unit of study (e.g., the number of neurons needed) and extrapolate to determine the maximum number of animals required.
problem: Sample size must be planned at the unit of study when it is not the animal
need: Power planning for nested designs (cells within animals) that returns animals needed

role: IACUC guidance page, audience: animal researchers at the University of Montana
