quote: The variability in the response variable expected between animals, frequently expressed as the standard deviation, with literature cited from which PI’s draw these conclusions. ... Using unrealistic statistical assumptions can result in inappropriate group sizes.
problem: PIs must justify SD and effect size from literature and often use unrealistic assumptions
need: Power tool that records the source of SD/effect size and shows sensitivity of n to those inputs

role: biostatistics shared resource workshop slides, audience: spatial omics users at UC Irvine
quote: 10 x 3 x 5000=150,000 data points, but only 10 TRUE biologically independent samples (mice) ... They treat cells as independent observations.
problem: Single-cell/spatial tests treat cells as independent, inflating false positives
need: Pseudobulk or mixed-model option that analyses at the animal level when cells are nested in mice

role: biostatistics shared resource workshop slides, audience: spatial omics users at UC Irvine
quote: Bad experimental design: Confounded batch effects with biological signals ... Disease samples → All in Batch 1
problem: Disease and control samples processed in separate batches
need: Design helper that balances groups across batches/days and warns when group and batch are confounded

role: consulting intake page, audience: Lund University researchers
quote: Can you formulate one main question or hypotheses without using the words ”and” or ”or”? ... How large effect do you wish to be able to interpret as statistically significant?
problem: Clients arrive without a single clear hypothesis or a target effect size
need: Start each analysis by recording the primary question and smallest effect of interest

role: consulting cheat sheet, audience: Purdue statistical consulting service consultants and clients
quote: A common population variance is usually assumed, to be estimated by the pooled sample variances. The default two-sample t-test implemented in the R function t.test() however does not assume a common population variance.
problem: Default t-test differs between software (pooled vs Welch), so p-values differ
need: State clearly which t-test variant is used and let users match other software

role: library research data guide, audience: University of Windsor researchers
quote: Assumptions of normality concern model residuals, the deviation of the observed values from the model-predicted values. Many of these models are robust to violation of the assumption of normality, particularly in large samples.
problem: Library test-choice guide has to correct the belief that raw data must be normal
need: Check normality on residuals and say so in the output

role: consulting FAQ, audience: Duke investigators using the BERD Methods Core
quote: Can you provide guidance on the study design and analytic methods so I can do my own analysis?
problem: Investigators want to run their own analysis after brief guidance
need: Tool that lets researchers execute an agreed analysis plan themselves with guard-rails

role: consulting FAQ, audience: Freie Universität Berlin students and staff
quote: In case of a thesis work, we assist you by the choice and realization of statistical methods. However, we do not perform the implementation ourselves.
problem: Students get advice but must implement the analysis themselves
need: Approachable tool to implement the advised analysis without coding

role: biostatistician's guidance page, audience: medical researchers (Vanderbilt biostatistics)
quote: Many authors and pharmaceutical clinical trialists make the mistake of analyzing change from baseline instead of making the raw follow-up measurements the primary outcomes, covariate-adjusted for baseline.
problem: Change-from-baseline scores are analysed instead of baseline-adjusted follow-up
need: Offer ANCOVA (follow-up adjusted for baseline) for pre/post designs instead of only change scores

role: biostatistician's guidance page, audience: medical researchers (Vanderbilt biostatistics)
quote: Categorization of continuous variables for analysis is inefficient at best and ... misleading and arbitrary at worst
problem: Continuous measurements are dichotomised (high/low) before analysis
need: Discourage splitting continuous variables and offer regression on the continuous scale

role: core facility consultation page, audience: users of the Viničná Microscopy Core Facility (Charles University)
quote: Clarify the specific numbers you wish to measure, the volume of data (e.g., 10, 100, 1,000 images), image sizes, preferred software, and any preliminary analysis attempts.
problem: Users come to the imaging core without defining what number to extract from images
need: Image-to-statistics workflow that starts by defining the measured quantity and its unit of analysis
